claims.statement: The Coding Agent Template is a Next.js 15 (Next 16.0.10) and React 19 application whose end-to-end purpose is to turn a natural-language prompt into a real code change on a Git branch: the user signs in, picks a repository and an agent CLI, and a background worker creates a Vercel Sandbox, runs the agent, and pushes the resulting commits back to GitHub.

The HTTP response is returned to the client before the work begins; all long-running work (branch-name generation, title generation, sandbox creation, agent execution, push) is delegated to next/server after(...) callbacks inside the POST /api/tasks route handler, and the tasks row in Postgres is the durable contract that bridges the synchronous API response and the asynchronous worker.

All routes require authentication; the supported providers are GitHub OAuth and Vercel OAuth (PKCE), and the enabled set is governed by the comma-separated NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_PROVIDERS env var parsed by getEnabledAuthProviders() in lib/auth/providers.ts, which defaults to GitHub-only when unset.

Per-user credentials (OAuth access tokens, per-provider API keys, and MCP connector env blobs) are encrypted at rest using AES-256-CBC under ENCRYPTION_KEY (lib/crypto.ts), and the session cookie is a JWE (A256GCM, alg: dir) signed with JWE_SECRET (lib/jwe/encrypt.ts and lib/jwe/decrypt.ts); both secrets are required and are never exposed via NEXT_PUBLIC_.

Six agent CLIs are supported — Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Google Gemini, and opencode — each implemented as its own module under lib/sandbox/agents/ and dispatched by executeAgentInSandbox via a switch on the AgentType union 'claude' | 'codex' | 'copilot' | 'cursor' | 'gemini' | 'opencode'.

Per AGENTS.md, all logger.* and console.* log statements in user-facing paths must use static strings only — dynamic values via template literals are forbidden because the log surface is returned to the UI — and redactSensitiveInfo() in lib/utils/logging.ts is a backup that scrubs known credential patterns from any string that does reach a log entry.

Per AGENTS.md, AI agents must never run development servers (pnpm dev, next dev, etc.) because they block the terminal; the validation gates a coding agent should use instead are pnpm format, pnpm type-check, pnpm lint, and pnpm build, all declared in package.json.
